title: Microsoft releases new Nvidia-chip AI PCs with revamped Windows 11
key_facts: On Wednesday 7 Oct 2026, at an event in San Francisco during Tech Week, Microsoft revealed the specs and prices of its Surface Laptop Ultra.

The Surface Laptop Ultra has two base models, from $2,600 and from $3,700 (the one with the more powerful chip), rising to $5,900 with more memory and storage; Microsoft says the top model is already out of stock.
Microsoft also revealed the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a developer workstation starting at $6,000, with dev tools such as VS Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, WSL and PowerShell 7.
A revamped Windows 11 includes a feature called Execution Containers, which Microsoft says makes it easier to sandbox AI agents; Satya Nadella said it will be available to all Windows 11 users.
Dell detailed its XPS 16 Creator Edition, available to preorder at Best Buy for $3,800 with delivery later in October.
Microsoft offers up to $1,000 off for people who trade in a MacBook Pro.
Nvidia had announced in June that it had agreements with Microsoft and other PC makers on AI-ready PCs built on its RTX Spark chip.
quote_evidence: The pitch for both this PC and workstation is that they are designed to run AI models on-device locally (and for free) with the CPU, GPU, unified memory, and other hardware modifications, like superior cooling, necessary to handle them.

Microsoft also revealed its new workstation powered by the RTX Spark chip: the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, which starts priced at $6,000 and comes equipped with Microsoft dev tools like VS Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, WSL, and PowerShell 7.
why_it_matters_hint: Prices and specs are now public for AI PCs aimed at developers, including those who use MacBooks today.
